The `slugify` function has been fixed. The issue was that the regex pattern `[^a-z0-9]` replaced each non-alphanumeric character individually, causing consecutive special characters (like `,`, space, `!`) to be replaced with multiple hyphens. 

The fix uses `[^a-z0-9]+` to match sequences of non-alphanumeric characters and replace them with a single hyphen, then strips any leading or trailing hyphens:

```python
def slugify(text):
    text = text.strip().lower()
    # Replace sequences of non-alphanumeric characters with a single hyphen
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", text).strip("-")
```
